proposal.description: While the converter runs, the OTP bit follows the live comparator instead of being set and held
proposal.reason: If OTP is recorded, the converter stops, the board cools and the supervisor restarts into S_SS before any host read, the OTP bit in fault_reg is cleared, although the header says bits are never cleared one at a time.

proposal.description: UVLO is not recorded while an overcurrent window trip is live, on the belief that an input droop under overcurrent is caused by the load current
proposal.reason: With the converter in S_SS or S_RUN, a UVLO that is asserted only while window_trip or window_trip_SS is high leaves fault_reg[1] clear, but OVERCURRENT is still recorded.

proposal.description: LATCH_ASSERT is not recorded once OVERCURRENT is in the record, on the belief that the window trip already explains the CPLD's latch trip
proposal.reason: When a window trip records OVERCURRENT and latch_assert rises on a later clock while the converter still runs, fault_reg[3] stays clear, so the OCP/SCP trip is missing from the record.

proposal.description: fault_time stamps the converter's soft start, read as the start of an operating episode, instead of the capture of the first fault cause
proposal.reason: fault_time is loaded with timestamp_ms on every S_SS clock while the record is empty. A first cause captured in S_RUN therefore reports the time soft start ended, and an empty record gets a non-zero fault_time after a clean start.

proposal.description: Over-voltage and over-current are confused in the bit map: OVP is placed in bit 0 and OVERCURRENT in bit 4
proposal.reason: An inferred analog OVP trip while running sets fault_reg[0], and an overcurrent window trip sets fault_reg[4]. The host reads each as the other.

proposal.description: The two overcurrent-related causes are confused in the bit map: LATCH_ASSERT (OCP/SCP) is placed in bit 0 and the window-trip OVERCURRENT in bit 3
proposal.reason: A window trip while running sets fault_reg[3], and the CPLD's latch_assert sets fault_reg[0], so a soft-start hiccup reads as a latch trip.

proposal.description: Over-voltage and under-voltage are confused in the bit map: OVP is placed in bit 1 and UVLO in bit 4
proposal.reason: A UVLO captured while the converter runs sets fault_reg[4] and reads as an analog OVP trip. An inferred OVP sets fault_reg[1] and reads as UVLO.
